_comment: MEASURED, NOT GUESSED (DIVE-8258, dev2, 2026-11-12). Before this file a connected Instagram read UNKNOWN on every box, and on a partner box nobody could ever turn it green (box bug 902). Logged OUT, /accounts/edit/ is answered by the SERVER with a 302 to /accounts/login/?next=… — the cookie decides it, not JavaScript. That login page carries Meta's current-user record with account 0 in its server-sent bytes (curl: 2 matches; the rendered page in a real Chrome at 1.5 s and at 8 s: 1 match), and its rendered form has a password field (<input type="password" name="pass">, 1 match at 1.5 s and at 8 s). So the marker does not wait for the app to draw: a logged-out probe matches even on the bare shell.

probe._comment: UNMEASURED HALF: no box or seat here holds an Instagram login, so the signed-in render of /accounts/edit/ was not observed. DIVE-8457 (box reports 942/974, partner client): the old marker's second half was any `type=password` input anywhere in the page, so a signed-in page that carried one read 'session expired' and the owner's Done reopened the sign-in window after a real sign-in. The signed-out reading is now the current-user record with account 0 (measured on every logged-out render) or the login form's own id (id="login_form", measured), never a bare password field. The signed-in reading is the same record with a non-zero account id, so a page that shows neither (a checkpoint, a 'browser not supported' page, a slow render) reads UNKNOWN and Done hands the site over as 'connected, not confirmed' (1.86.0) instead of asking for the sign-in again.
